Summary: Carousel spec does not address dynamic viewport resize crossing the fit/overflow threshold
Expected Behaviour: Spec should define whether carousel activates/deactivates on resize or only evaluates on initial load
Actual Behaviour: Req 8 AC 2-5 define static conditions (logos fit vs overflow) but do not specify runtime behaviour when viewport resize crosses the threshold between fitting and overflowing.
Status: Resolved — Req 8 AC 6-8 added for dynamic resize evaluation

Summary: Carousel Req 4 AC 3 adds object-fit: contain not present in original main spec Req 8 AC 3
Expected Behaviour: Minor traceability gap — carousel spec introduces a CSS detail the original requirement did not have
Actual Behaviour: Carousel Req 4 AC 3 specifies object-fit: contain which is new detail not in main spec Req 8 AC 3. Current implementation already uses contain so this is a documentation gap in the main spec not a conflict.

Summary: Carousel Req 6 AC 1 uses aria-roledescription which has limited screen reader support
Expected Behaviour: Spec should note that aria-roledescription support varies and recommend testing with actual assistive technology
Actual Behaviour: Req 6 AC 1 specifies role='region' with aria-roledescription='carousel'. Some screen readers ignore aria-roledescription and will only announce 'region' which may be less informative than intended.

Summary: Main spec Req 8 AC 3 says 5 logos but carousel spec and siteConfig both reference 7 — carousel spec does not note this deviation
Expected Behaviour: Carousel spec should explicitly note the deviation from main spec Req 8 AC 3 or main spec should be updated. BUG-131 tracks the main spec side.
Actual Behaviour: Carousel spec implicitly supports 7 logos via dynamic count (Req 8) but does not note the deviation from main spec Req 8 AC 3 which says 5 partner logo placeholders.
Status: Resolved — User removed Ashburton and Sygnia; carousel spec and siteConfig now both align with 5 logos matching main spec Req 8 AC 3

Summary: SSR hydration strategy causes video download on mobile before useEffect fires — contradicts Bugfix 2.2 and 2.5
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 2.2 says the system SHALL prevent the video file from being downloaded on mobile; Bugfix 2.5 says CSS display:none alone is insufficient as browsers may still download the video source
Actual Behaviour: Design Section 4 (SSR hydration strategy) defaults to rendering the video element on initial SSR render for all viewports. On mobile the browser will parse the <source> tag and initiate the 3.1MB download before useEffect fires and swaps to the fallback image. This violates the zero-download requirement for mobile.
Status: Resolved — Implementation uses useState(true) mobile-first default; SSR HTML never contains video on mobile

Summary: Design Correctness Property 1 does not cover Bugfix 2.2 (prevent download) — only covers DOM absence
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 2.2 requires the system SHALL prevent the video file from being downloaded; Property 1 only asserts the video element is absent from the DOM
Actual Behaviour: Property 1 validates DOM absence (2.1) and fallback image rendering (2.4/2.5/2.6) but does not assert that no network request for hero_video.mp4 is initiated. A test could pass Property 1 while still downloading the video if the element is removed after the download starts.

Summary: Design Correctness Property 2 does not cover Bugfix 3.3 (desktop poster fallback on video failure)
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 3.3 requires the poster fallback image to display when the video fails to load on desktop; Property 2 only validates attribute presence
Actual Behaviour: Property 2 validates attribute presence (autoPlay/muted/loop/playsInline/poster/aria-label) but does not assert that the poster image actually displays when the video source fails. The 'Validates: Requirements 3.3' claim is incomplete.

Summary: Design has no correctness property covering Bugfix 3.4 (mobile navy overlay over fallback image)
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 3.4 requires the navy overlay at rgba(20 28 66 0.55) to display on top of the fallback image on mobile
Actual Behaviour: Neither Property 1 nor Property 2 explicitly validates that the overlay renders on mobile. Property 2 mentions overlay preservation but scopes it to desktop (>768px). The overlay is mentioned in the Preservation Requirements prose but has no formal property.

Summary: Design has no correctness property covering Bugfix 3.5 (mobile heading/subtitle/CTAs unchanged)
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 3.5 requires heading subtitle and CTA buttons to continue displaying with mobile-responsive styling
Actual Behaviour: No correctness property validates that hero content (heading subtitle CTAs) renders identically on mobile after the fix. The Preservation Requirements prose mentions it but there is no formal property to test against.

Summary: Design has no correctness property covering Bugfix 3.6 (navy-dark fallback when image fails on mobile)
Expected Behaviour: Bugfix 3.6 requires navy-dark (#111b42) fallback background when the fallback image fails to load on mobile
Actual Behaviour: No correctness property validates the navy-dark background fallback scenario. The design mentions it in the CSS changes section ('The existing .hero background of var(--navy-dark) already provides the fallback') but does not formalize it as a testable property.

Summary: TC-452 expects aria-hidden on hidden video but design removes video from DOM entirely — test case conflicts with design approach
Expected Behaviour: Design says 'The video element is completely removed from the DOM on mobile so screen readers won't encounter it'; TC-452 checks for aria-hidden on a hidden video element
Actual Behaviour: TC-452 Step 2 inspects 'the hidden video element for aria-hidden=true or equivalent technique'. The design's conditional rendering approach means there is no hidden video element on mobile — it is absent from the DOM. TC-452 should be updated to verify DOM absence rather than aria-hidden.

Summary: Design does not specify where useIsMobile hook file should live — inline vs separate file is ambiguous
Expected Behaviour: Implementation guidance should specify the file location for the hook to avoid inconsistent placement
Actual Behaviour: Design Change 1 says 'inline or separate file' without a recommendation. For a hook used only by Hero.tsx inline is likely fine but the ambiguity could lead to inconsistent decisions across implementers.

Summary: Design Exploratory Test Case 2 uses 768px as 'mobile' but expected result description is wrong
Expected Behaviour: At 768px the viewport IS mobile (≤768px) so after the fix a fallback image SHOULD exist at 768px
Actual Behaviour: Exploratory Test Case 2 says 'Render Hero with matchMedia mocked to 768px — assert no fallback exists (will pass on unfixed code confirming missing fallback)'. The assertion is correct for unfixed code but the description 'Mobile Viewport No Fallback Image' is misleading — 768px is the boundary and the test name implies it is testing mobile behaviour when it is actually confirming the bug.

Summary: Design CSS specifies hover opacity: 0.6 but Carousel Req 4 AC 8 requires 0.7
Expected Behaviour: Carousel Req 4 AC 8 says logo SHALL reduce opacity to 0.7 on hover. Design should match the requirement.
Actual Behaviour: Design CSS .partnerLogo:hover uses opacity: 0.6 which contradicts the requirement. This perpetuates existing BUG-080 into the new carousel design rather than fixing it.
Status: Resolved — Partners.module.css uses opacity: 0.7; verified in final checkpoint

Summary: Design CSS preserves border-radius: 4px on logos which is not in the prototype or requirements
Expected Behaviour: Prototype has no border-radius on partner logos. Carousel requirements do not specify border-radius.
Actual Behaviour: Design CSS .partnerLogo includes border-radius: 4px carried over from current implementation (BUG-081). The design should either remove it to match prototype or document the deviation.
Status: Resolved — Partners.module.css has no border-radius; verified in final checkpoint

Summary: Design hook section contradicts Property 9 on ArrowRight keyboard direction
Expected Behaviour: Property 9 correctly states ArrowRight changes offset by -(logoWidth + gap). The hook Keyboard Navigation section should match.
Actual Behaviour: Hook section says ArrowRight: increments offset by logoWidth + gap (positive direction) but Property 9 says ArrowRight changes by -(logoWidth + gap) (negative). Since auto-scroll moves left (negative offset) ArrowRight should scroll content rightward (more negative offset). Property 9 is correct; hook description is wrong.
Status: Resolved — useCarousel.ts ArrowRight uses offset -= stepSize; verified in final checkpoint

Summary: Design no-JS fallback uses flex-wrap: wrap on .logoTrack which defeats horizontal scrolling
Expected Behaviour: No-JS fallback (Req 5 AC 1) requires a horizontally scrollable container. With flex-wrap: wrap logos wrap vertically instead of overflowing horizontally.
Actual Behaviour: Base .logoTrack has flex-wrap: wrap and .carouselContainer has overflow-x: auto. When logos exceed container width they wrap to the next row instead of creating horizontal overflow. The no-JS fallback needs flex-wrap: nowrap on the base track. Only the static mode (JS-enhanced logos fit) should use flex-wrap: wrap.
Status: Resolved — Partners.module.css base .logoTrack uses nowrap; .staticMode applies wrap; verified in final checkpoint

Summary: Design hook section says ArrowLeft decrements offset by -(logoWidth + gap) — double negative is confusing
Expected Behaviour: Hook description should use clear unambiguous language matching Property 9: ArrowLeft changes offset by +(logoWidth + gap)
Actual Behaviour: ArrowLeft: decrements offset by -(logoWidth + gap) is a double negative that equals incrementing by (logoWidth + gap). While the net result matches Property 9 the wording is misleading and could cause implementation errors.

Summary: Design Property 11 validates drag and keyboard under reduced motion but Req 6 AC 4 also requires swipe — swipe not mentioned
Expected Behaviour: Property 11 should validate drag AND swipe AND keyboard interactions under reduced motion with instant snapping
Actual Behaviour: Property 11 says drag and keyboard interactions should still change the offset but omits swipe. Req 6 AC 4 explicitly lists drag swipe or keyboard. The property should cover all three interaction types.

Summary: Design does not specify how gap responsiveness interacts with fit detection recalculation at 768px
Expected Behaviour: When viewport crosses 768px the gap changes (48px to 24px) which changes totalLogosWidth and may toggle carousel mode. Design should document this.
Actual Behaviour: Gap Responsiveness section says hook reads gap from computed style on ResizeObserver callback but does not state that a gap change at 768px triggers fit re-evaluation that could toggle mode. For 5 logos: 48px gap = 992px total; 24px gap = 896px total.

Summary: Design UseCarouselReturn.duplicationCount type suggests variable duplication but logic only uses 0 or 1
Expected Behaviour: Return type should use boolean (isDuplicated) or document that duplicationCount is always 0 or 1
Actual Behaviour: UseCarouselReturn has duplicationCount: number with comment 0=static 1=one extra copy. The number type implies arbitrary counts but the infinite loop logic only duplicates once. A boolean would be clearer.

Summary: Design CSS uses .jsEnhanced (camelCase) but Req 4 AC 6 suggests .js-enhanced (kebab-case)
Expected Behaviour: CSS Modules auto-scope class names so naming is internal but design should note the deviation from the spec suggestion
Actual Behaviour: Req 4 AC 6 says indicated by a CSS class such as .js-enhanced. Design uses .jsEnhanced (camelCase for CSS Modules). Technically fine but the inconsistency should be noted.

Summary: Design resolves BUG-136 in practice (keyboard instant snap under reduced motion) but does not note the spec deviation
Expected Behaviour: BUG-136 notes Req 6 AC 4 omits keyboard from reduced-motion instant snapping. Design extends it to keyboard without noting this as a spec interpretation.
Actual Behaviour: Design Keyboard Navigation section says With reduced motion: offset change is instant (no CSS transition Req 6.4) which extends Req 6 AC 4 beyond its literal text. Design should note this and recommend updating Req 6 AC 4.

Summary: No correctness property for Req 4 AC 7 (carousel occupies full container width)
Expected Behaviour: There should be a property or unit test verifying the carousel spans the full width of the Partners_Section container
Actual Behaviour: Req 4 AC 7 says carousel SHALL occupy full width. No correctness property validates this. Unit test Section retains visual identity does not explicitly check full-width.

Summary: No correctness property for Req 2 AC 1 always-on auto-scroll activation — Property 7 validates rate but not automatic activation
Expected Behaviour: There should be a property verifying auto-scroll activates automatically when entering scrolling mode
Actual Behaviour: Req 2 AC 1 says auto-scroll SHALL always be enabled when logos exceed viewport. Property 7 validates rate but assumes auto-scroll is already running. No property verifies automatic activation.

Summary: No correctness property for Req 4 AC 4/AC 5 responsive gap breakpoint at 768px
Expected Behaviour: There should be a property verifying gap changes from 48px to 24px at the 768px breakpoint
Actual Behaviour: Req 4 AC 4 and AC 5 define the gap breakpoint. No correctness property validates this. Property 4 uses gap as input but does not verify the gap value changes at the breakpoint.

Summary: Exploration test _viewportWidth parameter generated but never used — matchMedia mock does not vary per iteration
Expected Behaviour: Each fast-check iteration should use the generated viewport width to configure the matchMedia mock so the test truly varies behavior per width
Actual Behaviour: The _viewportWidth parameter is prefixed with underscore and unused; the matchMedia mock always returns matches: true regardless of the generated width. All 20 iterations test identical conditions.

Summary: Exploration test uses numRuns: 20 instead of design minimum 100 iterations
Expected Behaviour: Design doc and existing convention (BUG-050) specify minimum 100 iterations for property-based tests
Actual Behaviour: Hero.bugcondition.property.test.tsx uses numRuns: 20 for all three property assertions

Summary: Missing touch-action: pan-y on carousel container — touch swipe may trigger browser back/forward navigation or vertical scroll interference
Expected Behaviour: Carousel container should have touch-action: pan-y (or touch-action: none when dragging) to prevent browser default touch gestures from interfering with horizontal drag/swipe (Req 1.3 / 1.7)
Actual Behaviour: No touch-action CSS property is set on .carouselContainer or .jsEnhanced. On mobile browsers the horizontal swipe may conflict with browser navigation gestures or cause unintended vertical scrolling during diagonal swipes.

Summary: Missing user-select: none on carousel container during drag — text selection may occur on desktop drag
Expected Behaviour: Carousel container should prevent text selection during drag interaction to avoid visual artifacts
Actual Behaviour: No user-select: none is applied to the carousel container. While preventDefault() on pointermove helps it does not fully prevent text selection on all browsers especially during fast drags.

Summary: PartnersCarousel uses native instead of Next.js Image component — lint warnings present
Expected Behaviour: Next.js best practice requires using next/image for automatic optimisation (Req 14 AC 1)
Actual Behaviour: PartnersCarousel.tsx renders elements producing two @next/next/no-img-element lint warnings. Partner logos are static assets that would benefit from Next.js Image optimisation.

Summary: useCarousel hook hardcodes gap: 48 as initial ref value from options.gap but CSS may render 24px on mobile before first ResizeObserver fires
Expected Behaviour: Initial currentGapRef should match the actual rendered gap on first paint to avoid a brief incorrect fit calculation
Actual Behaviour: currentGapRef.current is initialised to options.gap (48) but on mobile viewports the CSS gap is 24px. Before the first ResizeObserver callback fires and reads computed style the hook uses 48px for any calculations which could briefly produce incorrect mode determination on mobile.

Summary: ResizeObserver callback uses stale entries array — debounced callback reads entries from the closure not the latest resize
Expected Behaviour: ResizeObserver debounced callback should capture the latest entry width not the entry from the first callback in the debounce window
Actual Behaviour: The ResizeObserver callback captures entries in the closure then debounces. If multiple resize events fire within 150ms only the first entries array is used. The last (most current) resize dimensions are lost. Should store latest width in a ref and read it in the debounced callback.

Summary: Duplicated logo alt text is identical to original — aria-hidden mitigates but alt should be empty string for hidden images
Expected Behaviour: Duplicated logos have aria-hidden=true but also have non-empty alt text. For aria-hidden elements alt should be empty string to be fully consistent
Actual Behaviour: PartnersCarousel.tsx duplicated images have alt={partner.alt} alongside aria-hidden=true. While aria-hidden prevents screen reader announcement the non-empty alt is redundant and could cause confusion if aria-hidden is ever removed.

Summary: Carousel Req 6 AC 1 specifies ARIA attributes only for scrolling mode but does not explicitly state they should be absent in static mode
Expected Behaviour: Spec should explicitly state that ARIA carousel attributes (role/aria-roledescription/aria-label) SHALL NOT be present in static mode
Actual Behaviour: Req 6 AC 1 says the carousel container SHALL have these attributes but does not scope to scrolling mode only. The implementation correctly omits them in static mode (Req 8 AC 3 implies this) but the spec should be explicit.

Summary: PartnersCarousel renders empty fragment <></> for zero logos instead of null
Expected Behaviour: Zero logos should render null for cleaner React tree — empty fragment adds an unnecessary node
Actual Behaviour: When logos.length === 0 the component returns <></> (empty React fragment). Returning null is the React convention for rendering nothing.

Summary: BUG-080 (hover opacity 0.6) and BUG-081 (border-radius 4px) are resolved by carousel implementation but not marked Resolved in bugs.csv
Expected Behaviour: BUG-080 and BUG-081 should be updated to Resolved since Partners.module.css now uses opacity: 0.7 and has no border-radius
Actual Behaviour: Partners.module.css carousel implementation uses opacity: 0.7 (fixing BUG-080) and removes border-radius (fixing BUG-081) but both bugs remain marked Open in bugs.csv.
Status: Resolved — BUG-080 and BUG-081 updated to Resolved in this audit

Summary: BUG-128 BUG-129 BUG-130 are resolved by siteConfig updates and carousel implementation but not marked Resolved
Expected Behaviour: BUG-128 (placeholder divs) BUG-129 (generic names) BUG-130 (5 entries) should be Resolved — siteConfig has 5 real brand entries and PartnersCarousel renders elements
Actual Behaviour: siteConfig.ts now has 5 real partner entries with correct names/paths. PartnersCarousel.tsx renders elements. These three bugs are functionally resolved but still marked Open.
Status: Resolved — BUG-128 BUG-129 BUG-130 updated to Resolved in this audit

Summary: Hover pause uses pointerenter/pointerleave which fire on touch devices — touch hover may incorrectly pause auto-scroll
Expected Behaviour: Hover pause should only apply to mouse/pen pointer types not touch. Touch devices should not trigger hover pause since there is no persistent hover state.
Actual Behaviour: useCarousel attaches pointerenter/pointerleave listeners without checking pointerType. On touch devices a tap triggers pointerenter which sets isHoveringRef=true. Since there is no reliable pointerleave on touch (finger lift may not fire it consistently) auto-scroll could remain paused after a touch interaction ends.

Summary: ENH-3 specifies removing only Ashburton and Sygnia from prototype but prototype has 7 logos with Discovery appearing twice (Discovery-300x167.png and Discovery-300x167_1.png in file listing)
Expected Behaviour: ENH-3 should account for all logo files in the prototype directory including the duplicate Discovery file
Actual Behaviour: ENH-3 AC 1 says 5 logos (Allan Grey / BrightRock / Discovery / Momentum / Ninety One) but does not mention the Discovery-300x167_1.png duplicate file in the prototype directory. Cleanup scope is incomplete.

Summary: ENH-6 prototype uses placeholder URL https://booking.example.com but AC 2 specifies real Calendly URL — no AC verifies the prototype itself is updated
Expected Behaviour: ENH-6 should include an AC or note requiring the prototype to be updated with the real Calendly URL for consistency
Actual Behaviour: ENH-6 Screen Requirements note says prototype uses placeholder but the Files to Change section is missing — no instruction to update prototype/index.html hero CTA href from booking.example.com to the Calendly URL

Summary: ENH-8 AC 3 specifies href /Tracking Budget 2026.xlsx with spaces but prototype uses Tracking-Budget-2026.xlsx with hyphens
Expected Behaviour: The href in the AC should match the actual filename. Prototype HTML uses hyphens; prototype directory has spaces in filename.
Actual Behaviour: ENH-8 AC 3 says link to /Tracking Budget 2026.xlsx (spaces). Prototype index.html line uses href='Tracking-Budget-2026.xlsx' (hyphens). Actual file in prototype/ is 'Tracking Budget 2026.xlsx' (spaces). The prototype HTML href does not match the actual filename.

Summary: ENH-10 does not specify what happens to the existing newsletterUrl export in siteConfig.ts
Expected Behaviour: ENH-10 Impact section notes newsletterUrl may become unused but no AC addresses cleanup or deprecation
Actual Behaviour: siteConfig.ts exports newsletterUrl which is currently used by Newsletter.tsx. ENH-10 replaces the external link with an inline form making newsletterUrl dead code. No AC covers removing or deprecating it.

Summary: ENH-10 does not specify error message text for failed submissions
Expected Behaviour: ENH-10 AC 11 says display an inline error message but does not define the error text content
Actual Behaviour: AC 11 requires an error message on failure but unlike the success state (which has defined text in the CSS spec) the error message text is unspecified. Implementers must guess the wording.

Summary: ENH-10 does not specify error state CSS styling
Expected Behaviour: ENH-10 Screen Requirements define success state CSS (.newsletter-success) but no error state CSS class or styling
Actual Behaviour: The success state has full CSS specification (colour / layout / icon). The error state has no CSS specification — no class name / colour / layout defined. Implementers must invent error styling.

Summary: ENH-10 AC 10 does not specify success confirmation message text
Expected Behaviour: AC 10 says display a success confirmation message but does not define the exact text
Actual Behaviour: The success state CSS references a confirmation text at font-size 0.9rem but the actual message wording (e.g. 'Thank you for subscribing!') is not specified in any AC.

Summary: ENH-10 does not address loading/submitting state for the newsletter form
Expected Behaviour: Contact form has a submitting state pattern but newsletter form has no AC for disabled button or loading indicator during submission
Actual Behaviour: Users could double-submit the form while waiting for the API response. No AC covers disabling the submit button or showing a loading state during the async Resend API call.

Summary: ENH-2 AC 6 says NavLink type needs CTA metadata but does not specify the exact property name or type
Expected Behaviour: AC 6 suggests 'e.g. a cta boolean or className property' but leaves the exact implementation ambiguous
Actual Behaviour: Two different approaches are suggested (boolean flag vs className string) without a recommendation. This could lead to inconsistent implementation decisions.

Summary: ENH-8 AC 2 specifies emoji prefix in button text but emoji rendering varies across OS/browsers
Expected Behaviour: Button text includes a Unicode emoji which may render differently or as a square on older systems
Actual Behaviour: The download button text includes an inbox tray emoji that relies on emoji support. No fallback is specified for systems that cannot render the emoji.

Summary: ENH-1 Screen Requirements omit responsive heading size reduction at 768px
Expected Behaviour: ENH-1 should note the responsive heading size reduction at 768px from the prototype
Actual Behaviour: Prototype styles.css @media 768px reduces .section-header h2 to 2.2rem. ENH-1 Screen Requirements only specify the desktop 3rem value without noting the mobile reduction.

Summary: ENH-10 newsletter form uses mailto: action in prototype but AC 7 specifies Resend API — prototype form action inconsistency not noted
Expected Behaviour: Prototype newsletter form has action=mailto: method=POST enctype=text/plain which differs from the Resend API specified in AC 7
Actual Behaviour: The prototype uses a mailto: form action as a no-backend solution. ENH-10 correctly specifies Resend API for production but does not note this prototype deviation or include updating the prototype form.

Summary: ENH-1 does not specify scroll reveal animation for testimonial cards
Expected Behaviour: Other sections (Blog / Social Feed) use ScrollReveal for fade-in animation per Req 12 AC 1. Testimonials cards have no animation AC.
Actual Behaviour: Req 12 AC 1 applies scroll reveal to content sections. ENH-1 does not include an AC for wrapping testimonial cards in ScrollReveal. This is inconsistent with Blog and SocialFeed card treatment.

Summary: No enhancement addresses updating existing test cases TC-003 / TC-010 / TC-027 that will fail after implementation
Expected Behaviour: TC-003 expects 5 nav links (becomes 6). TC-010 expects Get In Touch scrolling to #contact (becomes Book Appointment opening Calendly). TC-027 expects no inline form (will have one).
Actual Behaviour: Three existing passing test cases will fail after ENH-2 / ENH-6 / ENH-10 are implemented. The enhancements document does not note which existing tests need updating.

Summary: ENH-9 AC 6 specifies Content-Type header for Excel files but Next.js static file serving handles this automatically
Expected Behaviour: AC 6 is not independently testable — Content-Type is determined by the web server / CDN not by application code
Actual Behaviour: Next.js / Vercel automatically serves .xlsx files with the correct MIME type. This AC cannot fail due to application code and is not actionable by developers.

Summary: Req 4 Screen Requirements specify .btn-newsletter class on submit button but prototype uses unclassed button inside .newsletter-form
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should clarify whether the submit button uses the .btn-newsletter class or inherits styling from .newsletter-form button
Actual Behaviour: Prototype styles.css defines both .newsletter-form button (padding: 14px 32px) and standalone .btn-newsletter (padding: 16px 44px). Req 4 Screen Requirements say CSS class is .btn-newsletter with padding 14px 32px — mixing the class name from the standalone rule with the padding from the form rule.

Summary: Req 4 Screen Requirements Loading State specifies opacity: 0.6 and cursor: not-allowed but these values do not exist in prototype CSS
Expected Behaviour: Loading/disabled state values are production-only additions not derived from prototype
Actual Behaviour: Prototype styles.css has no disabled button styles. Requirements present opacity: 0.6 and cursor: not-allowed as screen requirements without noting they are production additions not prototype-derived.

Summary: Req 4 Screen Requirements Success State adds heading element with font-size: 1rem that does not exist in prototype
Expected Behaviour: Prototype .newsletter-success only has p elements at 0.9rem — no heading element
Actual Behaviour: Requirements add a heading 'Thank you for subscribing!' at font-size: 1rem font-weight: 500 that is a production enhancement. Should be noted as such.

Summary: Req 3 Screen Requirements .nav-cta transition list omits letter-spacing
Expected Behaviour: Transition should include letter-spacing or note the instant change is intentional
Actual Behaviour: The transition property covers background / color / border-color but .nav-cta letter-spacing changes from 0.06em (desktop) to 0.04em (mobile override) without transition.

Summary: Req 5 AC 10 references main spec Req 12 AC 1 but that AC only covers blog and feed cards not testimonial cards
Expected Behaviour: Req 12 AC 1 scope is 'blog cards and feed cards' — testimonials are a new addition to scroll reveal scope
Actual Behaviour: Req 5 AC 10 claims consistency with Req 12 AC 1 but actually extends its scope. Should note this as a new addition rather than an existing reference.

Summary: Req 6 AC 3 uses literal spaces in href but Screen Requirements say to URL-encode — inconsistency
Expected Behaviour: AC and Screen Requirements should use consistent href format
Actual Behaviour: AC 3: '/Tracking Budget 2026.xlsx' (spaces). Screen Requirements: 'Tracking%20Budget%202026.xlsx' (encoded). Functionally equivalent but inconsistent.

Summary: Req 2 Files to Change omits prototype/index.html — prototype hero CTA will retain placeholder URL
Expected Behaviour: Prototype should be updated to match production Calendly URL for accuracy
Actual Behaviour: Req 2 only lists src/components/Hero.tsx in Files to Change. Prototype hero CTA href remains https://booking.example.com. Previously identified as BUG-180.

Summary: Req 4 does not specify HTML escaping for user email in newsletter API email template
Expected Behaviour: Contact form API escapes user input (BUG-091 fix) but newsletter API has no equivalent AC
Actual Behaviour: Newsletter API will interpolate user email into HTML template. No AC requires escapeHtml() — security gap vs contact form pattern.

Summary: Cross-reference table omits Req 1 AC 5 (smooth-scroll targets) from affected ACs
Expected Behaviour: Req 1 AC 5 must include #testimonials as a smooth-scroll target
Actual Behaviour: Source doc ENH-2 Impact says Req 1 AC 5 must include #testimonials. Requirements doc Req 3 AC 2 defines the href but cross-reference table does not list Req 1 AC 5.

Summary: Req 4 does not specify honeypot spam protection for newsletter form
Expected Behaviour: Contact form has honeypot field (BUG-025 fix) but newsletter form has no equivalent
Actual Behaviour: API spec says 'same rate limiting and basic validation' but does not mention honeypot. Newsletter form is simpler (email only) but still vulnerable to bot submissions.

Summary: Req 4 error state CSS (.newsletter-error) and loading state CSS are production-only additions not in prototype
Expected Behaviour: Prototype has no .newsletter-error class or disabled button styles
Actual Behaviour: Requirements present these as screen requirements derived from prototype but they are entirely new production additions. Should be explicitly noted.

Summary: Req 1 AC 3 is a verification statement not a testable acceptance criterion
Expected Behaviour: AC 3 confirms prototype already has correct number — not an implementation action
Actual Behaviour: AC 3 states 'THE prototype footer SHALL already display the correct number'. This is a pre-condition check not an actionable requirement. Should be a Note.

Summary: Design doc Newsletter .btnNewsletter padding (14px 32px) conflicts with globals.css .btn-newsletter padding (16px 44px) — ambiguous which to use
Expected Behaviour: Design should specify whether the newsletter form button uses the CSS Module .btnNewsletter (14px 32px per prototype form button) or the global .btn-newsletter (16px 44px per globals.css)
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.3 defines .btnNewsletter with padding: 14px 32px matching prototype .newsletter-form button. But globals.css already has .btn-newsletter with padding: 16px 44px. Design does not clarify migration strategy — CSS Module class vs global class.

Summary: Design doc Newsletter component structure does not specify aria-label attribute on email input
Expected Behaviour: Req 4 AC 14 requires aria-label='Email address for newsletter' on the email input field
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.3 Component Structure lists 'email input' but omits the aria-label='Email address for newsletter' attribute required by Req 4 AC 14. The Screen Requirements in the requirements doc specify it but the design doc component spec does not.

Summary: Design doc Newsletter success state component structure underspecifies the subtitle text
Expected Behaviour: Req 4 AC 10 requires heading 'Thank you for subscribing!' and subtitle 'You'll hear from me soon.'
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.3 mentions 'Success state with green checkmark SVG heading and subtitle' but does not specify the exact subtitle text 'You'll hear from me soon.' in the component structure. The CSS spec references it but the JSX structure description is incomplete.

Summary: Design doc File Changes Summary omits prototype download button href fix from prototype file changes
Expected Behaviour: Prototype download button uses Tracking-Budget-2026.xlsx (hyphens) but actual file uses spaces — prototype href needs correction
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 6 Prototype Files table lists hero CTA href update and partner logo removal but does not include fixing the download button href from 'Tracking-Budget-2026.xlsx' to 'Tracking%20Budget%202026.xlsx'. This is a known issue per BUG-181.

Summary: Design doc newsletter API has independent rate limiter from contact API — combined abuse possible
Expected Behaviour: A single IP could send 5 newsletter + 5 contact requests per minute (10 total) since rate limiters are separate
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 5 duplicates the rate limiter Map from the contact route. Each route maintains its own counter. A determined abuser could send 5 requests to each endpoint within one minute. Design should note this as an accepted limitation or propose shared rate limiting.

Summary: Design doc newsletter form submission flow omits client-side email validation step
Expected Behaviour: Req 4 AC 12 requires validating email is non-empty and matches valid format before submission
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.3 Form Submission Flow lists: 1) prevent default 2) set submitting 3) extract email/honeypot 4) POST. No step for client-side validation. HTML required attribute provides basic check but AC 12 explicitly requires format validation before submission.

Summary: Design doc does not specify cleanup action for unused newsletterUrl export in siteConfig.ts
Expected Behaviour: Req 4 Note says newsletterUrl becomes unused. Design Section 6 lists it under 'Unused After Implementation' but no action specified.
Actual Behaviour: Design doc identifies newsletterUrl as unused but does not specify whether to remove it or add a deprecation comment. Implementer may leave dead code or accidentally break the import in Newsletter.tsx if not removed.

Summary: Design doc newsletter form honeypot HTML attributes not fully specified in component structure
Expected Behaviour: ContactForm honeypot uses tabIndex=-1 autoComplete=off aria-hidden=true. Newsletter design should mirror this.
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.3 mentions 'Hidden honeypot field (spam protection)' and has .honeypot CSS class but does not detail the HTML attributes: tabIndex=-1 autoComplete=off aria-hidden=true on the wrapper div. These are critical for the honeypot to work correctly.

Summary: Design doc does not address potential nav overflow with 6 items + CTA pill on medium viewports
Expected Behaviour: Current 5 nav links with 36px gap fit within 1100px. Adding Testimonials + wider CTA pill may overflow between 769px and ~1100px.
Actual Behaviour: Design doc does not specify whether the 36px gap needs adjustment or if a medium breakpoint is needed for 6 nav items. The CTA pill adds ~48px extra width (padding: 8px 24px). No responsive adjustment between 768px and max-width is specified.

Summary: Design doc .navCta transition description is ambiguous — could be interpreted as transition: all
Expected Behaviour: Prototype uses three individual transition properties: background color border-color. Design says 'all var(--transition)'.
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.1 says 'transition: background color border-color (all var(--transition))'. The parenthetical 'all' is ambiguous — could mean transition: all var(--transition) which would animate padding/border-radius changes. Should explicitly list three individual transitions matching prototype.

Summary: Design doc Testimonials section header class name .section-heading differs from prototype .section-header
Expected Behaviour: Production globals.css uses .section-heading. Prototype uses .section-header. Design should note this mapping for traceability.
Actual Behaviour: Design doc Section 4.4 correctly uses .section-heading (production class name) but does not note the prototype equivalent .section-header. Minor traceability gap for developers cross-referencing prototype.

Summary: Hero.preservation.property.test.tsx Property 4 block comment references old CTA text 'Get In Touch'
Expected Behaviour: Block comment should reference 'Book Appointment' to match the updated CTA text (ENH-6 Req 2 AC 1)
Actual Behaviour: Lines 209-210 say 'Both CTA buttons: Get In Touch (→ #contact)' but the actual assertion on line 244 correctly uses 'Book Appointment' with Calendly URL. Stale comment only — test passes correctly.

Summary: Requirements doc misses portrait alt text change — prototype says 'Independent Wealth Manager' but production says 'Financial Advisor'
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should capture every copy difference between prototype and production
Actual Behaviour: Prototype: alt='Keanu Le Roux, Independent Wealth Manager'. Production About.tsx: alt='Keanu Le Roux — Financial Advisor'. This branding change is not listed in the requirements doc.

Summary: Requirements doc misses blog post detail author title change — prototype says 'Independent Wealth Manager' but production says 'Financial Advisor'
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should capture every copy difference between prototype and production
Actual Behaviour: Prototype blog-post.html: author title 'Independent Wealth Manager'. Production BlogPostDetail.tsx: 'Financial Advisor'. File src/components/BlogPostDetail.tsx not listed in requirements.

Summary: Requirements doc misses blog post detail CTA text change — prototype has article-specific CTA but production has generic CTA
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should capture every copy difference between prototype and production
Actual Behaviour: Prototype blog-post.html CTA: 'Want to discuss how commodity movements affect your portfolio? I'd love to help you navigate these markets.' Production BlogPostDetail.tsx CTA: 'Ready to take the first step? I'd love to help you build a plan that works for your life and goals.'

Summary: Requirements doc misses blog post detail body content — prototype has full Gold/Oil article but production defaultPost has placeholder body
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should capture the full article body content for the default post
Actual Behaviour: Prototype blog-post.html has ~15 paragraphs of Gold/Oil article content. Production defaultPost.ts body has a single 'coming soon' placeholder paragraph. Change 4 only covers title/date/excerpt.

Summary: Requirements doc misses blog post detail excerpt difference — prototype detail page excerpt differs from landing page featured excerpt
Expected Behaviour: Requirements should note that the blog detail page excerpt is shorter than the landing page featured excerpt
Actual Behaviour: Prototype blog-post.html excerpt: 'Gold prices have fallen sharply even as the Middle East conflict has intensified. Normally war drives gold up. So what's going on?' (shorter). Landing page excerpt adds 'The short answer is oil.' at the end.

Summary: Change 10 does not explicitly state the current production title text — only says 'check if it matches'
Expected Behaviour: Change 10 should follow the same format as other changes with explicit 'Current production text' and 'New prototype text' fields
Actual Behaviour: Change 10 says 'Note: Check if the production <title> matches. If it still says Financial Advisor it needs updating.' Other changes explicitly quote both current and new text. Current production text is 'Keanu Le Roux | Financial Advisor'.

Summary: Change 6 does not specify how additional default posts integrate with Blog.tsx data flow
Expected Behaviour: Change 6 should clarify whether defaultPost.ts exports a single post or an array and how Blog.tsx consumes it
Actual Behaviour: Change 6 says 'Add 2 additional default posts to src/data/defaultPost.ts (or create a defaultPosts array)'. Blog.tsx currently imports { defaultPost } (singular) and wraps it in [defaultPost]. The parenthetical 'or create a defaultPosts array' is ambiguous — implementer needs clear guidance on the export shape.

Summary: 'No Copy Differences' table claims Blog heading/subtitle is identical but does not verify blog card 'Read More' link text
Expected Behaviour: Table should verify all text elements including link text within each section
Actual Behaviour: The table says 'Blog heading/subtitle: Identical' but the blog section also contains 'Read Full Article' and 'Read More' link text. These are identical between prototype and production but the table description is too narrow.

Summary: 'No Copy Differences' table does not list the blog post detail page (blog-post.html) as a section compared
Expected Behaviour: Table should include blog-post.html vs BlogPostDetail.tsx comparison
Actual Behaviour: The table only covers landing page sections. The blog post detail page has multiple copy differences (author title and CTA text and excerpt and body) that are missed because the detail page was not included in the comparison scope.

Summary: Design Change 13 hardcodes article-specific CTA text for all blog posts — regression for CMS posts
Expected Behaviour: CTA text should be generic or per-post; CMS blog posts about non-commodity topics should not show 'commodity movements affect your portfolio'
Actual Behaviour: Design §2.5 Change 13 replaces the generic CTA with Gold/Oil-specific text in BlogPostDetail.tsx. The design note acknowledges this but defers a ctaText CMS field to 'future enhancement'. All CMS posts will display commodity-specific CTA text which is semantically incorrect for non-commodity articles.

Summary: Design §4.3 testing impact does not enumerate specific affected test files — defers to a grep search
Expected Behaviour: Design should list the exact test files and assertions that need updating for implementer clarity
Actual Behaviour: Design says 'Affected test files should be identified by searching for import.*defaultPost.*from' but does not list the results. Actual affected files: Blog.unit.test.tsx (asserts 'Why Starting Early' text) and BlogPostDetail.unit.test.tsx (asserts 'Financial Advisor' title). Implementer must discover these independently.

Summary: Design does not address the blog detail page excerpt length discrepancy noted in requirements Change 4 / BUG-222
Expected Behaviour: Design should specify whether the detail page uses the same excerpt as the landing page or a shorter version
Actual Behaviour: Requirements Change 4 notes that blog-post.html uses a shorter excerpt than index.html for the same post. Design §2.2 defines a single excerpt field matching the longer landing page version. BlogPostDetail.tsx will render the longer excerpt on the detail page which differs from the prototype blog-post.html.

Summary: Design does not specify whether the old defaultPost.ts file should be renamed to reflect the plural export
Expected Behaviour: File is named defaultPost.ts (singular) but will export defaultPosts (plural)
Actual Behaviour: Design §2.2 changes the export from defaultPost to defaultPosts but the filename remains defaultPost.ts. While functional this creates a naming inconsistency. The design should explicitly state the file is not renamed to avoid confusion.

Summary: Design §4.3 mentions blog card count tests but does not verify whether such assertions actually exist in the test suite
Expected Behaviour: Design should confirm which specific test assertions will break rather than making general statements
Actual Behaviour: Design says 'Tests that assert on the number of rendered blog cards when using fallback data will now expect 2 cards (previously 0)'. Blog.unit.test.tsx does not appear to assert on card count for the fallback case — only that the featured article renders. The design's testing impact statement may be inaccurate.

Summary: Change 6 REVERTED per user decision — two card blog posts removed from defaultPosts array
Expected Behaviour: N/A — informational entry. Change 6 originally added 2 card posts ('Understanding Risk: Why Protection Matters' and 'Retirement Planning in Your 30s') to defaultPosts. User decided to revert; defaultPosts now contains only the featured Gold/Oil post. No card grid renders.
Actual Behaviour: defaultPosts array contains 1 element (featured Gold/Oil post only). Blog section shows featured article with no card grid below. Requirements.md and design.md both updated to mark Change 6 as REVERTED. TC-524 marked N/A.
